title: Expiry or lifetime stated beside a credential that offline text cannot verify
description: A credential shown with an expiry timestamp, a stated lifetime, or other expired-looking wording (for example an Expiration field or a note that a token lasts one hour), or a value of a family the provider issues as short-lived.
semantics: Offline text cannot establish current validity or revocation. A timestamp in or near the text states when the issuer says a credential stops working; it does not show that the time has passed on a reader's clock, that the value was not re-issued, or that the surrounding material is not the live one. Policy (maintainer-only, ADR 0020, ADR 0019 item 6): such text is expected to be flagged.

applicability.rationale: AWS temporary credentials (Expiration field) and GitHub App installation tokens (one hour) are the provider-documented short-lived forms read for this scenario. Further families are added after their pages are read.

evidenceBasis.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, ADR 0019 item 6 (#112)): text that states an expiry or lifetime beside a credential is expected to be flagged. Lifetimes are provider-documented (sources); the expectation is a project choice: offline text cannot establish current validity or revocation. It is not a claim about validity. Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history.

sources.supports: Temporary Credentials object carries AccessKeyId, SecretAccessKey, SessionToken and an Expiration timestamp 'on which the current credentials expire'.
ASIA-prefixed temporary access key ids are unique only in combination with the secret access key and the session token.
sources.locator: section 'Understanding unique ID prefixes', ASIA row

sources.supports: The installation access token will expire after 1 hour.
